nodes.doc: Theorem I.4: Concrete 2-cell Cauchy encode -> decode lossless roundtrip samples over GF(2^8).
nodes.signature: public theorem cauchy2_exact_roundtrip : cauchyDecode2 2 25 (cauchyEncode2 2 25 0x50 0xb7).1 (cauchyEncode2 2 25 0x50 0xb7).2 = (0x50, 0xb7) ∧ cauchyDecode2 11 14 (cauchyEncode2 11 14 0xde 0xad).1 (cauchyEncode2 11 14 0xde 0xad).2 = (0xde, 0xad) ∧ cauchyDecode2 3 24 (cauchyEncode2 3 24 0xff 0x01).1 (cauchyEncode2 3 24 0xff 0x01).2 = (0xff, 0x01)

nodes.doc: Theorem I.6 (Universal Cauchy 2x2 Non-Singularity Theorem): In ANY characteristic-2 field (including concrete `gf256Field`), for ANY distinct x0 != x1 and y0 != y1 with disjoint {x0, x1} ∩ {y0, y1} = ∅, the 2x2 Cauchy determinant (x0+y0)^(-1)(x1+y1)^(-1) + (x0+y1)^(-1)(x1+y0)^(-1) is STRICTLY NON-ZERO!
nodes.signature: public theorem gf_cauchy2_nonzero_det (x0 x1 y0 y1 : F) (hx : x0 ≠ x1) (hy : y0 ≠ y1) (h00 : x0 ≠ y0) (h01 : x0 ≠ y1) (h10 : x1 ≠ y0) (h11 : x1 ≠ y1) : K.add (K.mul (K.inv (K.add x0 y0)) (K.inv (K.add x1 y1))) (K.mul (K.inv (K.add x0 y1)) (K.inv (K.add x1 y0))) ≠ K.zero

nodes.doc: Theorem I.7 (Universal Cauchy 2x2 Exact Lossless Decoding Theorem): For ANY characteristic-2 field K, ANY disjoint distinct coordinates (x0,x1), (y0,y1), and EVERY payload pair (d0, d1), `cauchyDecode2K (cauchyEncode2K d0 d1) = (d0, d1)`!
nodes.signature: public theorem cauchy2_exact_decode (x0 x1 y0 y1 d0 d1 : F) (hx : x0 ≠ x1) (hy : y0 ≠ y1) (h00 : x0 ≠ y0) (h01 : x0 ≠ y1) (h10 : x1 ≠ y0) (h11 : x1 ≠ y1) : let (p0, p1) := cauchyEncode2K K x0 x1 y0 y1 d0 d1 cauchyDecode2K K x0 x1 y0 y1 p0 p1 = (d0, d1)

nodes.doc: Theorem I.8 (Concrete PLANARIA GF(2^8) Stratum-0 Universal Recovery): Instantiating Theorem I.7 on concrete `gf256Field` proves that PLANARIA's exact Stratum-0 `cauchyEncode2` / `cauchyDecode2` recovers EVERY `(d0, d1) ∈ [0..255]^2` from ANY two distinct surviving Stratum-0 cell coordinates `x0 != x1` in `{2..255}`!
nodes.signature: public theorem gf256_cauchy2_exact_decode (x0 x1 d0 d1 : Fin 256) (hx : x0 ≠ x1) (hx0_gt1 : x0.val ≥ 2) (hx1_gt1 : x1.val ≥ 2) : let (p0, p1) := cauchyEncode2 x0.val x1.val d0.val d1.val cauchyDecode2 x0.val x1.val p0 p1 = (d0.val, d1.val)

nodes.doc: Non-vacuity witness for Theorem I.8 (`gf256_cauchy2_exact_decode`): explicitly exhibits distinct coordinates `(2, 25)` and payload `(0x50, 0xb7)` satisfying every hypothesis and invoking the theorem directly.
nodes.signature: public theorem gf256_cauchy2_nonvacuous_witness : ∃ x0 x1 d0 d1 : Fin 256, x0 ≠ x1 ∧ x0.val ≥ 2 ∧ x1.val ≥ 2 ∧ (let (p0, p1) := cauchyEncode2 x0.val x1.val d0.val d1.val cauchyDecode2 x0.val x1.val p0 p1 = (d0.val, d1.val))

nodes.doc: Theorem II.1 (Mitosis Sufficiency): If a holographic bundle has N >= 2*k coded cells, a balanced disjoint bisection into floor(N/2) and N - floor(N/2) guarantees BOTH zero-overlap halves satisfy >= k and independently regenerate 100% of the bundle.
nodes.signature: public theorem mitosis_exact_sufficient (N k : Nat) (h : N ≥ 2 * k) : N / 2 ≥ k ∧ (N - N / 2) ≥ k

nodes.doc: Theorem II.2 (Tight Impossibility Lower Bound — Falsifiable Boundary): If N < 2*k, then NO disjoint bisection (a + b = N) can allow BOTH halves to recover >= k!
nodes.signature: public theorem mitosis_strict_impossibility (N k a b : Nat) (hN : N < 2 * k) (hPart : a + b = N) : ¬ (a ≥ k ∧ b ≥ k)

nodes.doc: Non-vacuity witness for Theorem II.2 (`mitosis_strict_impossibility`): for `N = 3 < 2 * 2`, the partition `1 + 2 = 3` satisfies all hypotheses and fails dual recovery.
nodes.signature: public theorem mitosis_strict_impossibility_witness : 3 < 2 * 2 ∧ 1 + 2 = 3 ∧ ¬ (1 ≥ 2 ∧ 2 ≥ 2)

nodes.doc: Theorem II.3 (Unaligned Arbitrary-Byte Cut Guarantee): An unaligned byte cut can bisect at most 1 physical cell across the cut boundary, reducing the balanced cell counts of a bundle by at most 1 per half in the worst case. Whenever N >= 2*k + 2, BOTH disjoint halves still guarantee >= k intact cells!
nodes.signature: public theorem mitosis_unaligned_cut_guarantee (N k : Nat) (h : N ≥ 2 * k + 2) : (N / 2 - 1) ≥ k ∧ ((N - N / 2) - 1) ≥ k

nodes.doc: Theorem II.4: Every single one of PLANARIA's 7 compiled bundles satisfies the strict unaligned-mitosis margin n >= 2*k + 4 (surviving even 50/50 cuts + boundary loss!).
nodes.signature: public theorem planaria_all_7_bundles_mitosis_safe : planariaBundleParams.all (fun p => decide (p.2 ≥ 2 * p.1 + 4)) = true

nodes.doc: Theorem II.5: Total PLANARIA cells = 192 <= 256 = 2^8 (exact Depth-8 Merkle tree fit), yielding pristine binary size 192 * 512 = 98,304 bytes (96 KiB).
nodes.signature: public theorem planaria_total_cells_exact : (planariaBundleParams.map Prod.snd).foldl (· + ·) 0 = 192 ∧ 192 ≤ 2 ^ 8 ∧ 192 * 512 = 98304

nodes.doc: Theorem II.6 (Exact Integer `PLACEMENT_SCHEDULE` Zero-Tie & Balanced-Halves Proof): Under `src/core/hbin.js`'s exact integer placement schedule `posNum(b, i, n_b)`: 1. Every bundle divides 480 cleanly (`480 % n_b = 0`), 2. ZERO cells across all 192 land on the midpoint `3360`, 3. Every bundle places EXACTLY `n_b / 2` cells strictly in `[0, 3360)` (left half) and EXACTLY `n_b / 2` cells strictly in `(3360, 6720)` (right half), 4. Every half strictly exceeds `k + 2` (so even unaligned cuts destroying 1 boundary cell still retain `>= k + 1` intact cells in BOTH halves!), 5. All 192 lexicographic `(posNum, bundleId)` sort keys are pairwise distinct.
nodes.signature: public theorem planaria_schedule_exact_halves : planariaIndexedBundles.all (fun (b, k, n_b) => let keys := bundlePosKeys b n_b let leftCnt := (keys.filter (fun p => decide (p < 3360))).length let midCnt := (keys.filter (fun p => decide (p = 3360))).length let rightCnt := (keys.filter (fun p => decide (p > 3360))).length decide (480 % n_b = 0) && decide (midCnt = 0) && decide (leftCnt = n_b / 2) && decide (rightCnt = n_b / 2) && decide (leftCnt ≥ k + 2) && decide (rightCnt ≥ k + 2)) = true ∧ all192LexKeys.length = 192 ∧ allDistinctSorted all192LexKeys = true

nodes.doc: Theorem II.6b (True `List.Nodup` + First-96 / Last-96 Sorted Index Bridge): 1. `all192LexKeys.Nodup`: proved formally via `msortFuel_perm` (no unverified sort gap!). 2. In the exact sorted `PLACEMENT_SCHEDULE` emitted into `.hbin` slots `0..191`, slots `0..95` ALL satisfy `posNum < 3360` and slots `96..191` ALL satisfy `posNum > 3360`!
nodes.signature: public theorem planaria_schedule_nodup_and_sorted_halves : all192LexKeys.Nodup ∧ let sorted := msortFuel 10 all192LexKeys sorted.length = 192 ∧ (sorted.take 96).all (fun key => decide (key / 8 < 3360)) = true ∧ (sorted.drop 96).all (fun key => decide (key / 8 > 3360)) = true

nodes.doc: Theorem II.7 (Exact 512-Byte Cell & Interleaved RS(254, 238) Byte Budget): 4B Sync + 508B Interleaved RS (2 x 254B) = 512B; 2 x 238B = 476B Authenticated Body = 16B Header + 332B Cauchy Shard + 128B (8 x 16B) Merkle Proof.
nodes.signature: public theorem planaria_cell_byte_budget_exact : 4 + 508 = 512 ∧ 2 * 254 = 508 ∧ 2 * 238 = 476 ∧ 16 + 332 + 128 = 476 ∧ 8 * 16 = 128

nodes.doc: Theorem II.8 (Disjoint Cauchy Coordinate Sets & GF(2^8) Fit): For all 7 bundles `(b, k, n)`, data coordinates `y ∈ [0, k)` and evaluation coordinates `x = k + i ∈ [k, k + n)` are disjoint and fit strictly inside GF(2^8) (`k + n <= 256`).
nodes.signature: public theorem planaria_cauchy_coord_disjoint : planariaBundleParams.all (fun p => decide (p.1 ≥ 1) && decide (p.1 + p.2 ≤ 256)) = true

nodes.doc: Theorem II.9 (Exact Raw Payload Capacity & 4x Holographic Expansion Ratio): Total source chunks across all 7 bundles = 48 (48 * 332 = 15,936 B raw payload capacity), yielding an exact 4:1 cell expansion ratio (192 / 48 = 4).
nodes.signature: public theorem planaria_payload_capacity_exact : let totalK := (planariaBundleParams.map Prod.fst).foldl (· + ·) 0 totalK = 48 ∧ totalK * 332 = 15936 ∧ 4 * totalK = 192

nodes.doc: Theorem II.10 (Two-Way Fragmentation Pigeonhole Law): If N > 2*(k - 1) cells are split arbitrarily into any two fragments a + b = N, at least one fragment MUST retain >= k cells and remain viable.
nodes.signature: public theorem pigeonhole_two_way (N k a b : Nat) (hk : k ≥ 1) (hN : N > 2 * (k - 1)) (hPart : a + b = N) : a ≥ k ∨ b ≥ k

nodes.doc: Non-vacuity witness for Theorem II.10 (`pigeonhole_two_way`): for Stratum-0 `N = 24, k = 2`, any partition `(12, 12)` retains at least one viable half.
nodes.signature: public theorem pigeonhole_two_way_witness : 2 ≥ 1 ∧ 24 > 2 * (2 - 1) ∧ 12 + 12 = 24 ∧ (12 ≥ 2 ∨ 12 ≥ 2)

nodes.doc: Theorem II.11 (Trisection Super-Additive Synergistic Recovery on Bundle 5 S3_ORGANISM_FX): Splitting Bundle 5's 40 cells (threshold k = 16) into 3 disjoint shards (13, 13, 14) leaves EVERY individual shard strictly non-viable for Stratum 3 (< 16), yet raw concatenation of ANY pair of shards yields >= 26 >= 16 cells, restoring 100% Stratum 3!
nodes.signature: public theorem trisection_synergy_recovery : let k := 16 let s1 := 13; let s2 := 13; let s3 := 14 (s1 + s2 + s3 = 40) ∧ (s1 < k ∧ s2 < k ∧ s3 < k) ∧ (s1 + s2 ≥ k ∧ s1 + s3 ≥ k ∧ s2 + s3 ≥ k)

nodes.doc: Theorem III.1 (Anastomosis Zero-Crash Progress Safety): For ANY damage pattern where Stratum-0 Stem Nucleus retains >= 2 cells, `resolveRenderer` ALWAYS resolves to a valid live executable target (NEVER `.deadCrash`), even if ALL higher strata (b1..b6 = 0) are completely obliterated!
nodes.signature: public theorem anastomosis_zero_crash_safety (p : ShardProfile) (h0 : p.b0 ≥ 2) : resolveRenderer p ≠ .deadCrash

nodes.doc: Theorem III.2 (General 6-Organ Anastomosis Zero-Crash & Non-Executable Isolation): When `b0 >= 2`, `resolveOrgan` NEVER crashes for ANY `(organId, maxStratum)`, and NEVER dispatches Bundle 0 (KERNEL) or Bundle 6 (GENOME) as an organ call target!
nodes.signature: public theorem resolveOrgan_zero_crash_safety (p : ShardProfile) (organId maxStratum : Nat) (h0 : p.b0 ≥ 2) : resolveOrgan p organId maxStratum ≠ .deadCrash ∧ resolveOrgan p organId maxStratum ≠ .execBundle 0 ∧ resolveOrgan p organId maxStratum ≠ .execBundle 6

nodes.doc: Theorem III.3 (Stratum Monotonicity under Cell Recovery): Recovering additional cells across any bundle NEVER degrades the resolved renderer stratum.
nodes.signature: public theorem anastomosis_monotonicity (p q : ShardProfile) (h0 : p.b0 ≤ q.b0) (h2 : p.b2 ≤ q.b2) (h3 : p.b3 ≤ q.b3) : (resolveRenderer p).rank ≤ (resolveRenderer q).rank

nodes.doc: Non-vacuity witness for Theorem III.3 (`anastomosis_monotonicity`): recovering Bundle 3 (`0 -> 8`) upgrades renderer rank strictly from S1 Wireframe (2) to S2 Cortex (3).
nodes.signature: public theorem anastomosis_monotonicity_witness : let p : ShardProfile := ⟨2, 0, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0⟩ let q : ShardProfile := ⟨2, 0, 4, 8, 0, 0, 0⟩ p.b0 ≤ q.b0 ∧ p.b2 ≤ q.b2 ∧ p.b3 ≤ q.b3 ∧ (resolveRenderer p).rank ≤ (resolveRenderer q).rank ∧ (resolveRenderer p).rank < (resolveRenderer q).rank

nodes.doc: Theorem III.4 (Monotone Fusion Dominance): Concatenating two disjoint damaged shards A and B yields an organism whose viability is ALWAYS >= max(viability(A), viability(B)).
nodes.signature: public theorem fusion_dominates_parents (a b : ShardProfile) : viabilityLevel (fuseDisjoint a b) ≥ max (viabilityLevel a) (viabilityLevel b)

nodes.doc: Theorem III.5 (Strict Super-Additive Synergistic Healing + Full 7-Bundle Regeneration): There exist two crippled sub-threshold shards A and B (each trapped at Stratum 1 / level 2 and unable to regenerate) whose raw concatenation A + B jumps all the way to full Stratum 3 AND satisfies `canFullRegenerate = true` across all 7 bundles including B6 GENOME!
nodes.signature: public theorem fusion_strict_synergy_exists : ∃ a b : ShardProfile, viabilityLevel a = 2 ∧ viabilityLevel b = 2 ∧ canFullRegenerate a = false ∧ canFullRegenerate b = false ∧ viabilityLevel (fuseDisjoint a b) = 4 ∧ canFullRegenerate (fuseDisjoint a b) = true ∧ viabilityLevel (fuseDisjoint a b) > max (viabilityLevel a) (viabilityLevel b)

nodes.doc: Theorem III.6 (Zero-Cliff Strict Separation vs BOTH RS(40, 16) AND Equal-Storage Flat RS(192, 48)): At ~12% survival (23 total cells out of 192), BOTH a single-stratum RS(40, 16) binary AND an equal-storage flat RS(192, 48) monolithic archive (same total payload capacity 48 chunks and same 192-cell storage budget!) are 100% DEAD (`false`), while PLANARIA remains strictly ALIVE (`viabilityLevel >= 1`, `resolveRenderer != deadCrash`)!
nodes.signature: public theorem zero_cliff_strict_separation : ∃ p : ShardProfile, p.totalCells = 23 ∧ cliffBinaryAlive p.b5 = false ∧ flatEqualStorageAlive p.totalCells = false ∧ viabilityLevel p ≥ 1 ∧ resolveRenderer p ≠ .deadCrash

nodes.doc: Spec-fidelity witness matching `src/core/hbin.js` Step 4: when `b2` (S1 Wireframe) is amputated (`b2 = 0`) while `b0, b1, b3, b4, b5` are viable, PLANARIA still achieves S3 (`viabilityLevel = 4`) via `b3` (S2 Cortex Render)!

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.0 (Byte-List Hamming Metric Triangle Inequality): For any three equal-length byte codewords `a, b, c`, `hammingDist a c <= hammingDist a b + hammingDist b c`.
nodes.signature: public theorem hammingDist_triangle : ∀ a b c : List Nat, a.length = b.length → b.length = c.length → hammingDist a c ≤ hammingDist a b + hammingDist b c | [], [], [], _, _ => by simp [hammingDist] | x :: xs, y :: ys, z :: zs, h1, h2 => by simp only [List.length_cons] at h1 h2 have ih := hammingDist_triangle xs ys zs (by omega) (by omega) simp only [hammingDist] by_cases hxy : x = y <;> by_cases hyz : y = z <;> by_cases hxz : x = z · simp only [hxy, hyz, ↓reduceIte]; omega · subst hxy; subst hyz; exact absurd rfl hxz · simp only [hxy, hyz, ↓reduceIte]; omega · simp only [hxy, hyz, ↓reduceIte]; omega · simp only [hyz, hxz, ↓reduceIte]; omega · simp only [hyz, hxz, ↓reduceIte]; omega · simp only [hyz, hxz, ↓reduceIte]; omega · simp only [hxy, hyz, hxz, ↓reduceIte]; omega | [], _ :: _, _, h1, _ => by simp at h1 | _ :: _, [], _, h1, _ => by simp at h1 | _ :: _, _ :: _, [], _, h2 => by simp at h2

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.1 (RS(254, 238) Singleton Distance & Unique Correction Radius): An MDS code with N = 254, K = 238 has minimum Hamming distance d_min = 17 and unique bounded-distance error-correction radius t = 8 bytes per codeword.
nodes.signature: public theorem rs254_238_unique_decoding_radius : let N := 254 let K := 238 let dMin := N - K + 1 let t := (dMin - 1) / 2 dMin = 17 ∧ t = 8 ∧ 2 * t + 1 ≤ dMin

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.2 (Unique Decoding Ball Disjointness via Real Byte-List Hamming Distance): If two distinct codewords `c1, c2` of equal length satisfy `hammingDist c1 c2 >= 2*t + 1`, NO received byte list `y` can lie within Hamming distance `<= t` of both `c1` and `c2`!
nodes.signature: public theorem rs_unique_correction_ball_disjoint (c1 c2 y : List Nat) (t : Nat) (hlen1 : c1.length = y.length) (hlen2 : y.length = c2.length) (hMinDist : hammingDist c1 c2 ≥ 2 * t + 1) : ¬ (hammingDist c1 y ≤ t ∧ hammingDist y c2 ≤ t)

nodes.doc: Non-vacuity witness for Theorem IV.2 (`rs_unique_correction_ball_disjoint`): two concrete 17-byte codewords at Hamming distance `17 >= 2*8 + 1` have disjoint radius-8 balls.
nodes.signature: public theorem rs_unique_correction_ball_nonvacuous : let c1 : List Nat := List.replicate 17 0 let c2 : List Nat := List.replicate 17 1 let y : List Nat := List.replicate 8 1 ++ List.replicate 9 0 c1.length = y.length ∧ y.length = c2.length ∧ hammingDist c1 c2 ≥ 2 * 8 + 1 ∧ ¬ (hammingDist c1 y ≤ 8 ∧ hammingDist y c2 ≤ 8)

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.3 (Interleaved 508-Byte RS(254, 238) Lane Partition Geometry): The 508-byte RS body after the 4-byte sync marker partitions into EXACTLY 254 even-offset bytes and 254 odd-offset bytes, each carrying 238 data bytes + 16 parity bytes.
nodes.signature: public theorem rs_interleaved_lane_geometry : countEven 0 508 = 254 ∧ countOdd 0 508 = 254 ∧ 238 + 16 = 254 ∧ 4 + 508 = 512

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.4 (2-Way Interleaved 16-Byte Contiguous Burst Recovery Guarantee): For ANY start byte offset and ANY contiguous burst error of length len <= 16 bytes, BOTH interleaved RS(254, 238) lanes receive <= 8 corrupted bytes — strictly within the exact unique correction radius t = 8!
nodes.signature: public theorem interleaved_burst_16_even_odd_bound (start len : Nat) (hlen : len ≤ 16) : countEven start len ≤ 8 ∧ countOdd start len ≤ 8

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.5 (Tight 17-Byte Negative Burst Lower Bound): For ANY start byte offset, a 17-byte contiguous burst ALWAYS drives at least one RS lane to 9 errors (> t = 8), proving 16 bytes is the exact tight burst-correction ceiling!
nodes.signature: public theorem interleaved_burst_17_exceeds_radius (start : Nat) : countEven start 17 > 8 ∨ countOdd start 17 > 8

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.6 (18-Byte Dual-Lane Saturation): For ANY start byte offset, an 18-byte contiguous burst pushes BOTH RS lanes to 9 errors (> 8).
nodes.signature: public theorem interleaved_burst_18_both_lanes_exceed (start : Nat) : countEven start 18 = 9 ∧ countOdd start 18 = 9

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.7 (Collision-Free Full Merkle Path & Leaf Commitment): Under a collision-resistant (injective) compression function `hashPair`, ANY two pairs `(leaf1, path1)` and `(leaf2, path2)` with identical left/right branch directions (`path1.map Prod.fst = path2.map Prod.fst`) that evaluate to the identical Merkle root MUST have BOTH identical leaves (`leaf1 = leaf2`) AND identical sibling paths (`path1 = path2`)!
nodes.signature: public theorem merkle_path_collision_free_binding (hashPair : Nat → Nat → Nat) (hInj : ∀ a1 b1 a2 b2, hashPair a1 b1 = hashPair a2 b2 → a1 = a2 ∧ b1 = b2) : ∀ (path1 path2 : List (Bool × Nat)) (leaf1 leaf2 : Nat), path1.map Prod.fst = path2.map Prod.fst → evalMerklePath hashPair leaf1 path1 = evalMerklePath hashPair leaf2 path2 → leaf1 = leaf2 ∧ path1 = path2

nodes.doc: Non-vacuity witness for Theorem IV.7: `pow2Pair` satisfies `hInj` universally over `Nat`.
nodes.signature: public theorem pow2Pair_injective : ∀ b1 b2 a1 a2 : Nat, pow2Pair a1 b1 = pow2Pair a2 b2 → a1 = a2 ∧ b1 = b2

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.8 (Byzantine Quarantine Zero-Contamination Theorem): Under cryptographic Merkle binding, EVERY cell accepted into the Cauchy MDS decoder after `merkleQuarantine` is guaranteed 100% authentic (ZERO Byzantine Trojans survive!).
nodes.signature: public theorem merkle_quarantine_zero_contamination (pinnedRoot : Nat) (cells : List HarvestedCell) (hBind : HashBinding pinnedRoot cells) : ∀ c ∈ merkleQuarantine pinnedRoot cells, c.authentic = true

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.9 (Zero False-Rejection of Authentic Cells): Every authentic cell in the input stream is preserved by `merkleQuarantine`, so Byzantine flooding can NEVER reduce the surviving authentic rank below k!
nodes.signature: public theorem merkle_quarantine_preserves_authentic (pinnedRoot : Nat) (cells : List HarvestedCell) (hBind : HashBinding pinnedRoot cells) : ∀ c ∈ cells, c.authentic = true → c ∈ merkleQuarantine pinnedRoot cells

nodes.doc: Non-vacuity witness for Theorems IV.8 & IV.9: a mixed authentic+Trojan stream satisfies `HashBinding 42` and filters cleanly to the exact 2 authentic cells.
nodes.signature: public theorem hashBinding_mixed_nonvacuous : let cells : List HarvestedCell := [⟨2, 42, true⟩, ⟨3, 999, false⟩, ⟨4, 42, true⟩] HashBinding 42 cells ∧ merkleQuarantine 42 cells = [⟨2, 42, true⟩, ⟨4, 42, true⟩]

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.10a (Order-Independent Unpinned Quorum Honest-Majority Election): For ANY insertion position (`pre ++ (honestRoot, honestCnt) :: suf`), if the honest lineage bucket has `honestCnt >= 2` and strictly outnumbers every competing bucket in `pre` and `suf`, `electUnpinnedQuorum` uniquely elects `some honestRoot`!
nodes.signature: public theorem unpinned_quorum_honest_majority (honestRoot honestCnt : Nat) (pre suf : List (Nat × Nat)) (hMin : honestCnt ≥ 2) (hPre : ∀ rc ∈ pre, rc.2 < honestCnt) (hSuf : ∀ rc ∈ suf, rc.2 < honestCnt) : electUnpinnedQuorum (pre ++ (honestRoot, honestCnt) :: suf) = some honestRoot

nodes.doc: Non-vacuity witness for Theorem IV.10a with the honest majority at a non-head index.
nodes.signature: public theorem unpinned_quorum_honest_majority_witness : electUnpinnedQuorum ([(999, 5)] ++ (42, 12) :: [(777, 3)]) = some 42

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.10b (General Arbitrary-List Unpinned Quorum Tie Fail-Closed): For ANY vote list containing two tied maximum buckets `(r1, c)` and `(r2, c)` with `c >= 2` at arbitrary positions (with all other buckets having count `<= c`), `electUnpinnedQuorum` unconditionally fails closed and returns `none`!
nodes.signature: public theorem unpinned_quorum_tie_fail_closed (pre mid suf : List (Nat × Nat)) (r1 r2 c : Nat) (hc : c ≥ 2) (hPre : ∀ rc ∈ pre, rc.2 ≤ c) (hMid : ∀ rc ∈ mid, rc.2 ≤ c) (hSuf : ∀ rc ∈ suf, rc.2 ≤ c) : electUnpinnedQuorum (pre ++ (r1, c) :: (mid ++ (r2, c) :: suf)) = none

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.10c (Sybil-Flood Override Counterexample): WITHOUT a pinned root, a Sybil attacker forging 36 cells under one coordinated fake root `999` against 24 authentic cells under `42` hijacks `electUnpinnedQuorum` to return `some 999`, proving formally why `pinnedRootHex` is required against majority-flood Sybil adversaries!

nodes.doc: Theorem IV.11 (Falsifiable Counterexample — Unauthenticated Decoder Contamination): Without `merkleQuarantine`, prepending even ONE single RS-valid Byzantine Trojan cell before authentic cells causes the naive first-k Cauchy window to contain a forged cell!
